details: Bitcoin (BTC) has been trading in a tight range, generally between $76,000 and $78,000, for several days, reflecting a period of market consolidation. This relative calm in Bitcoin has coincided with a notable rotation of speculative capital into AI-related altcoins. For instance, NEAR Protocol (NEAR) surged by over 20%, and Fetch.ai (FET) also saw significant gains, indicating a growing narrative around AI tokens within the crypto market. While Bitcoin navigates technical resistance around the $78,000 mark without a decisive breakout, some reports highlight bearish sentiment due to liquidations and weakening ETF demand.
title: Bitcoin Range-Bound as AI Tokens Lead Altcoin Rotation

details: The Ethereum ecosystem is experiencing a period of uncertainty, marked by high-profile departures from the Ethereum Foundation and the shutdown of some Layer 2 (L2) networks, such as Zero Network, after a relatively short operational period. This comes as Ether (ETH) tests critical support levels around $2,000-$2,100, a zone that many market participants are watching for potential reversals. Rising whale supply on exchanges suggests some profit-taking, although a slowdown in withdrawal transactions indicates that aggressive selling might not be dominating.
title: Ethereum Faces Uncertainty Amid Foundation Departures and L2 Shutdown

details: New legislation, dubbed the "Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Act," has been introduced by US lawmakers. The bill proposes the government acquire and hold a significant stash of Bitcoin, with some reports indicating a target of 1 million BTC and a mandated 20-year lockup period. This move aims to build a strategic financial buffer and signals a potential long-term embrace of Bitcoin by a segment of the US government, despite current market conditions.
title: US Lawmakers Propose Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Act

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has reportedly delayed a crucial exemption for tokenized assets, specifically concerning third-party tokens. This delay, cited by Bloomberg Law, stems from ongoing regulatory concerns about the classification and oversight of these digital assets. The decision could impact the development and adoption of tokenized securities within the US market, reflecting continued caution from regulators.
title: SEC Delays Exemption for Tokenized Assets

details: Cryptocurrency brokerage Blockchain.com has confidentially filed for an Initial Public Offering (IPO) in the United States. This move signals a continued trend of crypto firms seeking to go public and integrate further into traditional financial markets. The confidential filing indicates that the company is taking steps towards a public listing, which could provide more institutional access to the crypto space.
title: Blockchain.com Confidentially Files for US IPO
